utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was informed that between 96 and 103 victims were collected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me what happened then.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the afternoon, there was another meeting between the chief of the main staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, General Halilovic, and the chief of the main staff of the HVO, Brigadier Petkovic, and the subject discussed was the release of all prisoners. At this meeting, General Halilovic requested to see the persons who had been at the cinema, and I know that he went to the cinema, and I used that time for having a meeting with Brigadier Petkovic. At the office in my headquarters, I told him in detail about everything that I knew and everything that I had undertaken so far in respect of Ahmici, and I asked General Petkovic to have a meeting, by all means, with my associates and to support me in carrying out this investigation. I gave him -- I showed him an entire list of all the documents that we had, all the files, including these two orders that I spoke of related to the assistant for security, and I think it was around 17.00 or perhaps 17.30 at the maximum when Brigadier Petkovic had a meeting with the entire command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the meeting with you, what did General Petkovic say to your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Brigadier Petkovic said, first of all, that Ahmici was a crime and that that was very bad for the HVO, and I condemned this, and the investigation must go up to the end, to names and surnames. He said, "Your attitude towards civilians and detainees must be in the spirit of the Geneva Conventions, and you must have full cooperation with the International Red Cross, the UNHCR, and UNPROFOR." Further on, he said, "This area," he was meaning the Lasva River Valley, "we cannot and do not want to cleanse this area of non-Croats, and we shall not do that, but we have to defend it from all who are attacking us." He said, "The town is full of snipers, gangs, and the ordinary man in the street is tired of all of this, and they've had enough of all of this and they're waiting for this to be over. So take all measures to control these groups in this area, and they should not act as they wish to. Civilians have to be defended. Chaos is a folly for all. Let the military police arrest individuals. Your main attention should be focused on defence and on the positions because you're almost at the point where you have nothing to lose. You are encircled. Even several soldiers may be killed, but if a single civilian loses his life, that is a very bad thing." Then he said, "Can 20.000 Croats in Zenica attack 100.000 Muslims? In Konjic, we were attacked by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, from the back, while the HVO held the front line against the Serbs. None of you have the right to stop convoys of the International Red Cross, UNHCR, and UNPROFOR." So this is an outline of what General Petkovic said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, General, the conversation that you had separately from the command, the conversation you had with General Petkovic, how is that related to what Petkovic told them? Did Petkovic accept your positions? Was it your positions that came to the fore? Explain this to the Court. What kind of a conversation did you have with Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After I informed him, he accepted my positions, and he gave me full support then. At the meeting too, he emphasised this, as he met the command, and I knew that he had quite a problem because he didn't have much time. He was brought in UNPROFOR vehicles, and he had to go back, and he didn't have enough time to stay longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this separate conversation that you had, did you express to General Petkovic your suspicions as to within which units there could be those individuals, you were looking for the names and surnames, that might have committed the crime in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell him who you ordered to carry out an investigation and that this investigation was under way? Did you inform him about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed him about all the action that had been taken so far and about all the documents that I otherwise could not send him by mail because I didn't want to have it retyped. So I informed him of all the documents concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you didn't want to have these documents retyped. What did you actually have in mind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The letter of Colonel Stewart, the letter that I sent to Colonel Stewart, that is to say, all the documents that existed until then. They were shown to General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the original?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in the original. The original copies were shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that also mean the report from Ahmici and the orders that you gave on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I said "all documents." The orders, the reports, everything that had accumulated until then, all of it was made available to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Nobilo. General Blaskic, you said that you had communicated with Petkovic who, from your perspective, was suspected of involvement in the crime in Ahmici. You also spoke about the unit and the names. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Your Honour. I was talking about the unit, and I informed him that I had issued an order asking to have a list of names of the perpetrators submitted to me. I also asked General Petkovic, who was then a Brigadier, that at the meeting that he would have with my commanders, that he give support to this request so that the investigation would have to go all the way up to the names and surnames involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But General, you said specifically -- did you give -- did you tell Petkovic the name of the unit?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was engaged in that area? Yes, I did mention that to Brigadier Petkovic. I mentioned this to Brigadier Petkovic through the reports too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, you mentioned the military police. You mentioned the military police here. Therefore, did you tell Petkovic that the unit was the unit from the military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That it was my suspicion that individuals from that unit had done it, that that was my suspicion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So you told Petkovic that you suspected certain individuals from the military police. That's what you said expressly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The military police was in that area, engaged in that area, and my suspicion was that some individuals from that unit were engaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Did you also mention some names, names of individuals?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not mention any names. Brigadier Petkovic knew who the commander of the military police was, and until then, through the reports from the assistant for the security service, I did not receive any names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us define this. I think we didn't and we should have. The battalion of the military police, how many soldiers does that involve?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The battalion of the military police is about 300, up to 700 or 500 soldiers. I did not have it directly under my control so that I would know, and directly under my command, but it shouldn't be less than 300 or more than 700 soldiers. So 300, perhaps 500.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think that it was opportune, lawful, and to the point to blame the entire unit or were you looking for individual responsibility?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's not the way I was brought up and educated at the academy, that I should seek collective responsibility. It always had to be individual responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, there was a discussion on the petrol station Kalen. That is a very interesting question. Please tell us, what happened earlier on, what happened that day, and then afterwards, about the Kalen station, which is very telling in its own right.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was a strange problem, and there were many such which were illustrative of the prevalent chaos at the time. On that day, the mayor of Vitez --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What day are you referring to? The 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the 30th of April. I was informed that a special purpose unit had militarily captured the petrol station Kalen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which special purpose unit?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Vitezovi Special Purpose Unit, that they had captured the Kalen petrol station and that they were distributing and selling petrol at that station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, when they captured it, who was the owner of that station, and what did petrol mean in those days? What was its value?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the information I received from the mayor, I think it was captured either on the 16th or the 17th of April, that is, this petrol station. The owner was a Bosniak Muslim. I think his surname was Kalen. Probably that was his name. I'm sure, however, that he was a Bosniak Muslim. As to what petrol meant in those days, I can illustrate by the fact that we would allot ten litres per brigade, and at the station, there were several thousand litres of petrol, and this petrol was being sold by members of the Vitezovi Special Purpose Unit, and the mayor asked for my assistance to put an end to illegal business. I first required from the commander that he restore the station to the competence of the civilian and military authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which commander?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The commander of the Vitezovi Special Purpose Brigade, Mr. Kraljevic. He refused. Then I wrote a report to the head of the defence department in Mostar and briefed him on the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you, as the commander of the Operative Zone to whom the Vitezovi unit was resubordinated on that day, why are you writing to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the only measure left to me because I had no other authority. This is something that the commander of the Vitezovi Special Purpose Unit was aware of because he himself said that he was directly subordinated to the defence department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, in the course of these proceedings, you said that the mayor told you that the Vitezovi had captured the station on the 16th or the 17th, but in the course of these proceedings, from the testimony of members of the British Battalion, did you remember when exactly that petrol station was captured? During these proceedings here, not according to your recollection, but according to the testimony here in court.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps it was at dawn on the 16th of April but I'm not a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is that petrol station? Could you just tell us? Describe the place.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the main Vitez-Busovaca road. The main road is south of the village of Krcevine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which side?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: North in relation to the town of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a crossroads there? Is there an intersection of roads?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there is a cross-section there, one road going to Vjetrenica and Zenica and the other to Krcevine and Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a bear there, a stuffed bear at that petrol station?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm not sure. I couldn't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never mind. So you write to the commander of the Vitezovi and what did you ask him to do?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked him what the mayor had asked of me, and that is that the unit should return the captured petrol station to the civilian municipal authorities. I received an answer from the defence department for my information, in which he ordered the commander of the Vitezovi to return to the municipal authorities the captured petrol station. In the course of the day, that is what he did. Only a day later -- actually, he returned it fictitiously, but then he came to see me with a decision of the municipal authorities, which stated that the municipality was giving him the petrol station. I realised then, and I later checked, that even the order of the head of the defence department had not been carried out, but, in fact, the situation remained unchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Santic came to complain to you and asked you to intervene in Mostar, that they order the Vitezovi to return the petrol station, and then he makes a gift of that station to the Vitezovi. Did you establish how it came about that Santic changed his mind all of a sudden?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked him how this had happened, and then he told me that he had been forced to put the issue on the agenda of a government meeting, and to take such a decision, and that he had no other choice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he was forced. Do you mean that he was threatened by force?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have here a rather interesting situation regarding the functioning of the chain of command of the resubordinated units. Let us focus on that for awhile. The Vitezovi were resubordinated to you, and yet you had to contact their commander for him to give them an order. Tell the Court, when a unit is attached to you, to what extent do you become their commander? Is there a part of the command function that you never assume? Will you explain that, both with regard to the police and the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When a unit is attached to me, I am in command for the deployment of that unit for a particular task. Once the task has been accomplished, the unit goes back to its regular functioning, but even with regard to the implementation of a task, the commander is aware that he does not have such command authority as he has over his own regular units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what is it that is lacking in this case and that is present in relation with your own unit, even when you're deploying the military police or the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never have authority for sanctioning, authority for logistics support, or some other authority that I have over my directly subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you replace a commander, even during deployment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that would be unfeasible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, would you say that the 4th Battalion of the military police was deployed by you or with your authority in or around Ahmici on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It had already been stationed in the Bungalow without my authority. It was stationed there before. But patrolling as a daily duty along the Vitez-Busovaca-Travnik road, as a daily task, was under my authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would the whole battalion have been present in Ahmici on the 16th of April or part of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not the whole battalion, and how many of them would be there, that depended on the battalion commander, but not all of it. There were some military policemen securing the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One last question: From your observations of Ahmici after the event, would you be able to help this Court by giving us your judgment as to whether it was possible for what was done at Ahmici to have been done by some, only of the military police who were there, without the knowledge or support of the other military police who were also there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The area is quite large, but without any knowledge hardly, but maybe in view of the kind of terrain involved, it could be possible because the front line was there, and there was fighting between the BH army, but certainly a number of them knew what the perpetrators did. Maybe not all of them knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One last question if I may. General, when did you first suspect that some members of the military police might have done what was done at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the first time, when I received the first report from Colonel Bob Stewart. That means on the 22nd of April, '93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I would like to add to something that my colleague said. During the meeting of the 30th of April, you informed General Petkovic about your concerns that the military police was implicated, at least some of the people were. At the same meeting, General Petkovic apparently said that the military police had to arrest the criminals, and the military police reported to General Petkovic. How do you explain that then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the discussion when Brigadier Petkovic spoke about violence and crime in Vitez and about armed gangs that were looting, he said that the military police must arrest individuals. Unfortunately, that military police was not subordinated to General Petkovic either but to the defence department and the head of the administration for defence in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Was he present at that meeting, that commander, I don't remember his name, that is, the commander of the military police, was he present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that because it was a meeting of the members of the command of the Operative Zone, which mean members of the command of the Operative Zone were present. He wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General Blaskic, you have already said here that you didn't agree with the position within the organisational structure of the military police. I think that I'm right when I say that.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, of both the military police and the special purpose units, I never agreed with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But speaking now about the military police, why did the people who decided, who chose this type of organisation, this model of organisation, do you have some idea of why they chose that because we are now checking to see whether you were right. One could have an organisation which, in and of itself, cancels itself out and would represent a risk for you, that you could be a very good General, theoretically speaking, as Judge Jorda already referred to in his question, that's theoretically, but when you look at all of your orders from a theoretical point of view, we would not have so many problems, but we know that, in fact, there were problems. Why do you think the people chose that model? Was it a way to "divide and conquer" or was it something else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, I never agreed with such a model of organisation, and this increased my command impotence, and with an army structured in that way, you're asking me why such a model was created. In my view, one of the reasons could be that they didn't know what kind of model they were developing, but I discussed this, and we will see later on that I wrote about the negative effects of such a model on my command powers. So if they didn't know, they could have changed that model. It is hard for me to tell what the other reason was, but in any event, I believe that such reasons existed. To hold a unit of 500 men directly connected, could provoke behaviour contrary to the positions of the command that I was in charge of. In my talks with representatives of the UN, I tried to explain this. I had a single responsibility and multi-level commands. I asked for that to be changed. What the real motive was, I can only assume. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, once the model had shown itself not to be effective, was there somebody who suggested that the model be changed or was there not, or did you make that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and I managed to change that model. Unfortunately, not soon enough. I could go on, I could elaborate on this, but I was the one who had proposed a change of the model, and I succeeded eventually, but it took more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Perhaps at another time, Mr. Nobilo, we will go back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next week, we will show how the special purpose units were abolished, as well as the autonomy of the military police and what a major undertaking that was, but in order to deal with this crucial issue comprehensively, I would suggest that document D523 be shown to the witness, but now we're going to have a small break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we will take a 10-minute or 15-minute break, and then we will work until 1.30, which will allow the General, who is not only answering the questions of his attorney but responding to the questions of the Judges' curiosity in respect to very important points in the case. All right. We'll take a 10-minute to 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please be seated. Please continue, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As I already said, we would like to have D523 shown to the witness, please, and after that, D518, but that is a document that is under seal, so that is why we would like to move into private session when we examine that document. But now we're examining D523; could you please place it on the ELMO? Another article, number 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That article was not translated, the one that is of interest to us. All right. I can read it too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Document D523 is part of the rules of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I'm not sure that I understood that. You were mentioning a document. Has that already been tendered? I suppose it has been because it has a number. Is it a new exhibit, 523?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's right. D523, but only Article 10 was translated, but Articles 8 and 9 were not translated, and they are part of the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. I think that the Prosecutor is going to make an objection, first of all, to say that he doesn't have the translation and then say that they only translated two relevant articles and that the context is not there. I'm making the objection for you to speed things along.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, these are two short articles, and we tendered this a few months ago as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. What I suggest is the following: The interpreters have taken an oath. I suggest that we continue to work. Mr. Nobilo will read the article which he thinks is relevant, but your objection has been noted, Mr. Kehoe, and I ask the registrar to ensure that in the next few days, the entire document be translated. We know that the accused will not have to come back because he's here, he is the accused, and then he can explain if there is a problem in that area. Let me remind you, Mr. Kehoe, that you've got all the time that you need for your cross-examination. Do you agree with that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Having both objected and answered, I don't have to go any further. I leave it to you now, that is, the work of reading the relevant articles that you feel are necessary for the demonstration of your argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Document D523 is part of the rules of the military police which was admitted in document 518 and which we tendered a few months ago, and we gave it to the Prosecutor too. I'm going to read Articles 8 and 9. The title is "Chapter 2, Control and Command." So this is the rules of the military police.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'd like a clarification. Is this D523 or are we going to start with 518, because if we do, we would have to move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No. It's the 518 which is covered by seal. That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We're now talking about D523; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We will listen to the translation, but please read it slowly so that the interpreters can do a proper job.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's right, and we've placed on the ELMO what I'm reading in the Croatian version so the interpreters have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The title is "Control and Command. Article 8: All units of the military police are subordinated to the administration of military police of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna under the control and command of the chief of administration of the military police. Article 9: In carrying out daily operational military political tasks, the units of the military police are subordinated to the commander of the military district, i.e., to the highest ranking commander of the HVO in the area of responsibility of the units of the military police." Now I would like to move into private session, and we are going to see a document concerning the military police where you can see this much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If I've understood things correctly, the administration of the military police answers to the defence department but that the other part is under -- the operations depend on the operational commander. I would like you to be very careful here. Would you please reread Article 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. After that, I suggest that we put a question to the Colonel, for him to explain. It is not operations, it is daily operational tasks. We will read it out. "In carrying out daily operational military police tasks --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The word "daily," I don't have that in my translation. That's why there was a very valid objection by the Prosecutor. We're not talking about daily things. Mr. Nobilo, I'm very serious now. I always am, in fact, even if I smile sometimes. Ahmici is behind all of this. We want to know about the military police in its operations. We're not talking about daily activities. I would like to have the article reread very slowly and translated once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's quite wrong. I did not add "daily operative military police tasks." That's exactly what it says here, that is to say, in carrying out daily/operative military police tasks, and now I'm going to ask the Colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are daily/operative military police tasks? Explain this, Colonel. Then it's all going to be clear to you from the next document.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, these are patrols, then securing command posts, work at command blockade points, and all other daily military police tasks, like bringing in military conscripts, et cetera, that is to say, daily, day-to-day things that the military police is engaged in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. It's done on a current basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did I understand you and the witness to be drawing a distinction between daily military duties, as you have described them, and employment in the course of an armed confrontation with the enemy? I would take it that your position is that they would be subordinated to you in the latter situation only; is that it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the other situation, according to orders of the head of the defence department, they would be attached to me because in Article 8, Your Honour, it says that "all units of the military police are subordinated to the administration of the military police," and that is under the control and command of the chief of administration of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I propose the following, Your Honour: The next document is going to clarify all these dilemmas. With your permission, I would like to suggest this, and it is truly going to deal with all the dilemmas concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I asked you to be patient. Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. Nobilo, this is the time to clarify another question that I had asked beforehand. Who decided to establish the military police under those terms? Who did that? Who established it on these terms, that is, going back to the question and by putting the organisation within the organisational chart in a way that all reasonable people would not agree with. Who decided that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know the name and surname. I know the structure. I know who was the head of the defence department. I know who was the chief of the main staff. But who passed the decision on this kind of structure, that, I do not know, but I know that the head of the defence department, the first head of the defence department, was Mr. Bruno Stojic, that the next Minister of Defence was Mr. Perica Jukic, that the commander in chief was Mr. Mate Boban, but who reached the decision to organise it -- to organise the military police and the special purpose units in this way, so wrongly, I don't know who stands behind that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: The other question is the date. What date was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The HVO was first established, as far as I know from the documents, from the 8th of April, 1992. When the military police of the HVO specifically was established, I think that this will be shown in certain rules or something, but I don't know the exact date, exactly when the military police of the HVO was established because I never worked in the military police of the HVO, in 1992 at any rate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In any case, we will see the date because I think we can understand or at least perhaps understand the reasons if we put ourselves in the political and social conditions which may have given reason for that. In any case, we will see that afterwards. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, the document then should be done in a private session, is that right, 518? (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 1.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of March, 1999, at 2.00 p.m.
